Issued at 222 AM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Ridging in the process of folding overhead as a shortwave crashes 
ashore in the Pacific NW, complete with impressively deep moisture 
plume that has actually produced appreciable rainfall amounts as far 
south as southern California. Closer to home, surface high pressure 
continues to hold down the fort, leading to another quality day 
across the region... and exquisite conditions for those looking to 
make the trek on foot across Mighty Mac this morning. Moisture 
advection will be on the increase heading through the day as that 
Pacific borne system forces its way into the region. As such, may 
see a touch more in the way of cloud development across the region 
this afternoon, but nowhere near enough to drum up any rain. Highs 
today top out in the mid 70s to low 80s again... but with the 
increased moisture advection, overnight lows will rise a touch in 
comparison to the last couple nights, likely settling in the 50s to 
lower 60s near the lakes. 

As we venture into Tuesday, the wave will have already ejected into 
the Dakotas and Canadian Prairies, with robust surface cyclogenesis 
response anticipated. Deeper moisture plume to begin nosing into our 
neck of the woods as the surface low commences occlusion through the 
day. Associated surface cold frontal boundary to provide forcing to 
our north and west. Should be noted that most areas likely stay dry 
through Tuesday evening, with the exception likely being eastern 
upper and far NW lower into the Straits. Better moisture 
concentration commences through the evening into the overnight, 
which will be when potential for rain reaches its zenith. Have some 
doubts about convective potential owing to a lack of instability... 
but nonetheless, if we can attain a convective element to things 
Tuesday night, could see some localized heavy rain outbursts as flow 
will slowly become parallel to the front, thus slowing its advance 
and opening a door for some training convection within a +3.0 sigma 
anomaly PWAT environment. Anticipation is that the front clears 
Wednesday, which would leave us in the dry slot of the cyclone... so 
ideally we should see a drying trend, but may need to watch for dry 
slot convection later in the afternoon if upper forcing permits. 

The biggest story to come from this system very well could be its 
wind field, as a pinched pressure gradient between the broad surface 
low over Ontario and the surface high pressure over New England 
support an accelerating wind field... As mentioned by previous 
forecaster, wind fields just off the deck generally hold 20 to 30kts 
(locally up to 35kts). Warm advection processes Tuesday may stunt 
mixing potential, but within the dry slot on Wednesday, ample mixing 
should support a gusty W to WSW wind, perhaps pushing 40mph along 
the immediate lakeshores... generally 25 to 35mph elsewhere. 

The system departs by Thursday, forcing in a cooler airmass to the 
region... but the outer edge of the windfield will remain overhead, 
thus bringing about a much more autumnal feel as highs generally 
hold in the 60s and struggle to break 70 south amid breezy NW winds. 
Backside moisture will depart for Thursday, so anticipation is some 
poofy diurnal cumulus clouds and not much else. Heading into the 
weekend, temperatures quickly rebound to the mid 70s to low 80s 
Friday and Saturday amid a brief zonal flow regime. Quick shortwave 
passages may support unsettled weather through the weekend before a 
strong cold front is forced through the region by the conclusion of 
the weekend... bringing potential for a sharply cooler airmass to 
intrude for the start of next week. Current long term guidance shows 
highs in the mid 60s to near 70. Yes it may feel a bit chilly, but 
should be noted that by mid September average highs do start to drop 
below 70 in spots... so at this juncture, the upcoming cooldown 
looks to be seasonable and not so much anomalous.
